neighbours.label: the point in an empirical-research sentence where the data source is being introduced ('Using | a new data set of', 'used | data on 3,635', 'the National | … Survey', 'field | surveys'); its output promotes ' data', ' randomized', ' administrative'. 'Using'/'used' with a tool, and 'National' in a museum or team name, stay quiet
fire: Drawing on the National Health Interview Survey, the paper tracks smoking rates over two decades.
The economists used data on 12,000 workers to measure the effect of the minimum wage.
Using a new panel data set of 900 villages, we study how roads change school enrolment.
Our estimates come from the National Survey of Family Growth, which interviews adults every year.
Using district-wide data, the authors compare test scores before and after the reform.
The sociologists used survey data on 5,400 couples to examine who does the housework.
Respondents were sampled from the National Education Longitudinal Study of eighth graders.
Using a new data set of 2,300 loan applications, the study tests for bias in lending.
quiet: Standing outside the National Portrait Gallery, the guide talked about painters for two hours.
The carpenters used a crane on the roof to lift the heavy beams.
Using a new set of kitchen knives, we chopped vegetables for the whole village.
Our seats were behind the national anthem singers, who perform at every match.
Using a borrowed ladder, the neighbours cleaned the gutters before the storm.
The economists were surprised by the award and thanked their families.
Visitors were welcomed at the National Railway Museum by former train drivers.
Using an old family recipe, the bakery makes two thousand loaves a week.

notes: Card: ' National' x4, ' used' x3, ' national' x2, ' using' x2, ' Using', ' field', '-wide', all introducing the data of a study (Using a new data set of assassination attempts, used data on 3,635, National Health and Nutritional Examination Survey, province-wide data, field surveys); logit effect promotes ' random', ' randomized', ' administrative', ' data'. Probes: 'drawn from the National Longitudinal Survey of' 0.60, 'Using a new data set of 4,000 households' 0.30, 'field surveys' 0.29, 'Using province-wide data' 0.28, 'used data on 2,500 patients' 0.25, 'administrative records from Swedish tax registers' 0.18; 'Using a sharp knife' 0.008, 'used a hammer' 0.008, 'National Gallery' 0.01, 'researchers … were pleased with the award' 0.02. Fire strengths sit close to the 0.20 bar, so the median is at risk.
